Issued at 213 AM MDT Wed Aug 26 2026

2AM satellite water vapor imagery shows two features that will 
influence the weather across Wyoming over the next 5 days. The first 
feature is an upper high centered over New Mexico and it's 
associated ridge axis positioned roughly along the western Wyoming 
border. Today, the ridge axis is forecast to remain in it's current 
location (far western Wyoming) with an embedded shortwave 
disturbance rounding it this afternoon. There will be enough 
moisture aloft for isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms 
as the disturbance passes through. The location and initiation of 
showers and thunderstorms will be very similar to what occurred 
Tuesday afternoon and evening. That is convective initiation across 
the higher elevations of central and southwest Wyoming. Showers and 
thunderstorms are forecast to then shift east into the Green River, 
Bighorn, and Wind River Basins and into Sweetwater, Natrona, and 
Johnson Counties. However, chances of any of the aforementioned 
locations seeing a shower or thunderstorms are anywhere from 15 to 
30 percent. Although coverage is expected to be less today due to 
weaker forcing aloft, gusty 45 to 60 mph outflows will be possible 
in any shower or thunderstorm. This is due to DCAPE values upwards 
of 1500 J/kg, a classic inverted-V sounding, and 40 to 45 degree dew 
point depressions. Shower and thunderstorm chances exist between 1PM 
and 9PM. A few lingering showers are possible across northwest 
Wyoming through midnight as the ridge begins to shift east. With the 
ridge largely overhead and 12 to 14C 700mb temperatures, expect 
widespread highs in the 80s, with a few locations reaching 90.

As mentioned previously, there is another feature present on 
satellite water vapor imagery and that is a trough currently off the 
Pacific Northwest Coast. By late tonight, this trough will begin to 
move onshore the Pacific Northwest and slowly help shift the upper 
ridge across Wyoming. The ridge will shift east across Wyoming 
through late Thursday. Flow on the upstream side of the ridge will 
become more southwesterly across the state as the eastern shift 
occurs. A shortwave disturbance, and an associated surface front, is 
forecast to move across Wyoming Thursday afternoon and evening. Deep 
available moisture will also begin to increase with this disturbance 
and front with PWATs in the 0.75" to 0.90" range (95th percentile of 
climatology) across west and northwest Wyoming. With all this in 
mind, showers and thunderstorms are forecast across the 
aforementioned areas Thursday afternoon and evening. Gusty 50 to 60 
mph winds and frequent lightning will once again be the primary 
threats with any convection. Localized heavy rainfall is possible 
with the higher PWATs, however, storms are expected to be moving 
with 25 kt+ cloud layer winds. Thus, the flooding threat is rather 
low at this time. Thursday's high temperatures across western 
Wyoming are forecast to be right around 80 degrees and in the mid 
80s to low 90s elsewhere across the state.

Ensemble guidance is in consensus that the ridge will be over the 
central CONUS and the upper trough be positioned over the Pacific 
Northwest on Friday. This ultimately places Wyoming in deep 
southwest flow with increasing Pacific moisture. Ensemble guidance 
is signaling that, by Friday afternoon, PWATs will exceed the 97th 
percentile of climatology. Southwest flow will only strengthen as 
the aforementioned trough slowly shifts east into the Intermountain 
West on Saturday. Additionally, embedded shortwaves are expected to 
traverse the state Friday and Saturday afternoon. This means that an 
active Friday and Saturday are forecast, especially across western 
Wyoming due to being in better proximity to the abundant moisture. 
As the forecast currently stands, a front will begin trekking across 
the state late Friday through midday Saturday. This front will be 
the focus of widespread showers and thunderstorms during this 
timeframe across west and northwest Wyoming. There is currently a 45 
to 50 percent chance of at least 0.5" of rain from Friday night 
through Saturday night across northwest Wyoming. It is important to 
note that these details are bound to fluctuate as we get closer to 
Friday and more HI-Res model guidance becomes available. Regardless, 
this will need to be monitored over the coming days for moderate to 
heavy rainfall and any localized flooding. Temperatures on Friday 
are forecast to be comparable to Thursday across the area. Behind 
the front on Saturday, high temperatures are forecast to be 7 to 15 
degrees cooler than Friday.

There is consensus that the Pacific Northwest trough and low will 
push east into the Northern Rockies on Sunday and provide support 
for another front to trek across the state. However, there are 
differences among deterministic model guidances on the exact 
trajectory of the low and the amount of associated moisture.
